world.title: Texas executes Jamaal Howard after courts reject lethal-injection appeals
world.summary: Texas executed Jamaal Howard, 46, by pentobarbital injection Wednesday night at the Huntsville state prison. He was the 30th person executed in the United States this year and the first since Tennessee’s failed attempt to execute Christa Pike on Sept. 30. Howard was convicted of fatally shooting convenience-store clerk
world.content: Texas executed Jamaal Howard, 46, by pentobarbital injection Wednesday night at the Huntsville state prison. He was the 30th person executed in the United States this year and the first since Tennessee’s failed attempt to execute Christa Pike on Sept. 30. Howard was convicted of fatally shooting convenience-store clerk Vickie Swartout during a 2000 robbery in Silsbee. He apologized to her family before the injection. Howard’s lawyers asked Texas courts and the U.S. Supreme Court to halt the execution, arguing that the drug used on Pike posed similar risks to Howard and that he was intellectually disabled. The courts rejected the requests without explanation. Texas told the Supreme Court that Howard’s lawyers had not supplied evidence meeting the legal standard for an intellectual-disability claim. Pike survived two pentobarbital doses and regained consciousness days later. Her lawyers said she remains seriously ill, and a Tennessee judge ordered officials to preserve evidence from the failed execution. Texas has two more executions scheduled for November. Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee suspended the state’s remaining execution this year while an investigation proceeds.
world.image_alt: Texas executes Jamaal Howard after courts reject lethal-injection appeals

world.title: US prepares torture charges against Maduro and wife over detained Americans
world.summary: U.S. prosecutors were expected to bring new charges against ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, over the alleged torture of more than a dozen Americans detained in Venezuelan prisons during his rule, a U.S. official and people familiar with the investigation said. Prosecutors were als
world.content: U.S. prosecutors were expected to bring new charges against ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, over the alleged torture of more than a dozen Americans detained in Venezuelan prisons during his rule, a U.S. official and people familiar with the investigation said. Prosecutors were also considering charges against others accused of involvement. The announcement could come as soon as Thursday, Oct. 8. U.S. forces seized Maduro and Flores in Caracas on Jan. 3 and brought them to New York, where they face separate drug-trafficking and weapons charges. Both have pleaded not guilty. Their lawyers are challenging the prosecution, arguing that Maduro has immunity as a former head of state and that his capture was unlawful. A judge has not ruled on the immunity motions. Flores was due in federal court Thursday to seek release to house arrest. Her lawyers cited health problems, while prosecutors opposed release on flight-risk and public-safety grounds. The couple’s trial is scheduled for June 2027.
world.image_alt: US prepares torture charges against Maduro and wife over detained Americans

world.title: EU presses China to curb car exports as trade talks test ties
world.summary: European Union trade chief Maroš Šefčovič began two days of talks in Beijing on Oct. 8 with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, seeking to narrow a trade deficit that Brussels says exceeds €1 billion a day. The EU wants a pilot arrangement to address the rapid growth in Chinese hybrid-car exports. Beijing has reject
world.content: European Union trade chief Maroš Šefčovič began two days of talks in Beijing on Oct. 8 with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, seeking to narrow a trade deficit that Brussels says exceeds €1 billion a day. The EU wants a pilot arrangement to address the rapid growth in Chinese hybrid-car exports. Beijing has rejected voluntary export limits, and the negotiations also cover access to critical minerals and European companies’ access to China’s market. The discussions follow consultations launched in June and an EU call for tangible progress by October. Brussels argues that subsidized imports and barriers to European firms are increasing pressure on industrial sectors. China says trade restrictions would be protectionist and has threatened to respond if the EU targets Chinese goods or companies. Šefčovič is due to report to EU leaders at their Brussels summit on Oct. 15-16, where trade with China is a central agenda item. France and Germany are urging the bloc to prepare a mechanism to respond rapidly to economic threats; Beijing has urged them to avoid protectionist measures.
world.image_alt: EU presses China to curb car exports as trade talks test ties

world.title: German far-right AfD wins state parliament presidency in historic first
world.summary: Saxony-Anhalt’s state parliament elected Tobias Rausch of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) as its president on Oct. 6, the first time since the Nazi era that a far-right politician has led a German state legislature. He received 48 votes to 29, with five abstentions. The AfD and the Sahra Wagenknecht Allianc
world.content: Saxony-Anhalt’s state parliament elected Tobias Rausch of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) as its president on Oct. 6, the first time since the Nazi era that a far-right politician has led a German state legislature. He received 48 votes to 29, with five abstentions. The AfD and the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) together hold 44 seats; the secret ballot left the source of the four additional votes unclear. The result followed the AfD’s 43.8% vote share in the Sept. 6 state election, which gave it 39 seats but not a majority. Chancellor Friedrich Merz called Rausch’s election a historic break and said anyone voting for the AfD was undermining the credibility of his party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU). He also cautioned against assuming the extra votes came from CDU lawmakers because the ballot was secret. State lawmakers are expected to vote to elect a regional premier in December. AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund will need support beyond his party, and the BSW has not committed to backing him.
world.image_alt: German far-right AfD wins state parliament presidency in historic first

world.title: UK keeps East Jerusalem diplomatic mission open under new name
world.summary: Britain says its East Jerusalem consulate will continue operating as the “UK Mission, Jerusalem,” after Israel’s 30-day deadline to close it expired Thursday. Workers removed the consulate signs, but the British flag remained. The two governments now describe the building’s status differently. Foreign Secretary Ed Mili
world.content: Britain says its East Jerusalem consulate will continue operating as the “UK Mission, Jerusalem,” after Israel’s 30-day deadline to close it expired Thursday. Workers removed the consulate signs, but the British flag remained. The two governments now describe the building’s status differently. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Britain does not accept Israel’s authority to close it and that the mission will continue serving Palestinians. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said the consulate had ended operations and that 20 British diplomats, including the consul general, would leave Israel. Israel has authorized seven diplomats to remain at the building with a “very limited” scope of activity. Britain says it will rebuild its presence after temporarily withdrawing some staff and their families for security reasons. The order followed British measures against Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, including a ban on settlement goods. Israel disputes that the settlements are illegal; the UN and most countries regard them as such. Miliband ruled out reciprocal action against Israeli diplomats while talks continue. The separate British embassy in Tel Aviv is unaffected.
world.image_alt: UK keeps East Jerusalem diplomatic mission open under new name

world.title: Thousands protest Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of Brazil
world.summary: Thousands of people joined a student-led march in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday, Oct. 7, to protest the prospect of Flávio Bolsonaro becoming president. He led Brazil’s first-round vote with 47%, compared with incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s 45%. The two will meet in a runoff on Oct. 25 because neither won
world.content: Thousands of people joined a student-led march in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday, Oct. 7, to protest the prospect of Flávio Bolsonaro becoming president. He led Brazil’s first-round vote with 47%, compared with incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s 45%. The two will meet in a runoff on Oct. 25 because neither won more than half the vote. Marchers called for “Never Again Bolsonaro” and voiced fears about the far right returning to power. They cited Flávio’s support for amnesty for his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his 2022 election defeat. Protesters also raised concerns about Flávio’s promised spending cuts and their possible effects on universities and social programs. Ahead of the runoff, Flávio is seeking conservative alliances and promoting a smaller state and tax changes, while Lula has turned to social media and consulted leftist influencers who won legislative seats.
world.image_alt: Thousands protest Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of Brazil

world.title: France suspends stun grenade use after student loses hand; protests continue
world.summary: France has suspended police use of stun grenades at student protests after a 15-year-old lost his hand during a confrontation in Lens on Monday. Unions called for further demonstrations Thursday. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the suspension would last until investigators establish what happened. Accounts differ
world.content: France has suspended police use of stun grenades at student protests after a 15-year-old lost his hand during a confrontation in Lens on Monday. Unions called for further demonstrations Thursday. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the suspension would last until investigators establish what happened. Accounts differ on whether police fired the device at the boy or he picked it up before it exploded. Students, unions and rights groups accused police of excessive force. Nuñez said 18 incidents had been referred to the police inspectorate, while Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu denied that security forces had been ordered to confront young protesters. More than 500 schools were fully or partly closed Wednesday, and student and teacher unions called for more marches Thursday. Lecornu said the government would present initial proposals by the end of October on school repairs, teacher availability and other student demands, but gave no details. He said he wanted “concrete, quick and fully funded answers”. The protests began over staff shortages and school conditions and have expanded into a nationwide movement.
world.image_alt: France suspends stun grenade use after student loses hand; protests continue

world.title: Evicted Spanish pensioner Maricarmen Abascal dies as housing protests intensify
world.summary: Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old pensioner whose eviction from her Madrid home sparked nationwide housing protests, died in hospital on Wednesday, the Madrid Tenants’ Union said. She had lived in the apartment for more than 70 years. Police and social workers removed her on a stretcher on Sept. 23, and she was taken
world.content: Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old pensioner whose eviction from her Madrid home sparked nationwide housing protests, died in hospital on Wednesday, the Madrid Tenants’ Union said. She had lived in the apartment for more than 70 years. Police and social workers removed her on a stretcher on Sept. 23, and she was taken to hospital. Her eviction prompted protests over rents and tenant protections. The company that owned the apartment later agreed she could return, but the union said the arrangement came too late. Demonstrations and a protest camp in Madrid’s Puerta del Sol continued after her death, while unions called a nationwide general strike for Nov. 11. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for Nov. 29 after lawmakers rejected two emergency housing decrees. His Cabinet approved a replacement package on Tuesday. With Parliament dissolved, the package is due to go before the permanent council of Congress.
world.image_alt: Evicted Spanish pensioner Maricarmen Abascal dies as housing protests intensify

business.title: UK Conservatives pledge to exempt family homes from inheritance tax
business.summary: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch pledged to exempt family homes from inheritance tax and allow couples to pass on an additional £1 million tax-free if her party returns to government. She said the change would more than halve the number of families paying the tax; the Conservatives estimate it would cost about £6 b
business.content: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch pledged to exempt family homes from inheritance tax and allow couples to pass on an additional £1 million tax-free if her party returns to government. She said the change would more than halve the number of families paying the tax; the Conservatives estimate it would cost about £6 billion a year from 2029-30. Badenoch said the party could not abolish inheritance tax altogether while also funding defence, prisons and deficit reduction. The Conservatives say £83 billion in savings, including welfare and overseas-aid cuts, would fund their wider spending plans, while the Liberal Democrats allege a £33 billion shortfall. Labour and Reform UK said the inheritance tax proposal would chiefly benefit wealthy households. An earlier Conservative pledge to raise the threshold for family homes was not implemented after the party entered government in 2010.
business.image_alt: UK Conservatives pledge to exempt family homes from inheritance tax

business.title: Oil and rising Treasury yields pull Wall Street off record highs
business.summary: U.S. stocks fell Wednesday, retreating from records set a day earlier. The Dow Jones fell 0.66% to 51,180, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each lost 0.22%. Renewed gains in oil prices and rising Treasury yields weighed on shares as investors assessed the risk that higher energy costs could keep inflation elevated and rais
business.content: U.S. stocks fell Wednesday, retreating from records set a day earlier. The Dow Jones fell 0.66% to 51,180, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each lost 0.22%. Renewed gains in oil prices and rising Treasury yields weighed on shares as investors assessed the risk that higher energy costs could keep inflation elevated and raise borrowing costs for companies and the government. A strong $39 billion auction of 10-year Treasury notes helped ease losses. Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s September meeting showed officials saw scope for another rate increase before year-end, though traders saw little chance of a move at the October meeting. Major U.S. banks are due to begin reporting third-quarter earnings next week; analysts cited by Protothema forecast S&P 500 earnings growth of about 25% from a year earlier.
business.image_alt: Oil and rising Treasury yields pull Wall Street off record highs

business.title: EU presses China to curb exports as trade talks open in Beijing
business.summary: The European Union opened two days of trade talks with China in Beijing on Oct. 8, seeking steps to narrow a record trade gap and ease pressure on European industries from rising Chinese exports. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is meeting Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao as Brussels pushes for product-specifi
business.content: The European Union opened two days of trade talks with China in Beijing on Oct. 8, seeking steps to narrow a record trade gap and ease pressure on European industries from rising Chinese exports. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is meeting Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao as Brussels pushes for product-specific import quotas and “tangible” results before an October deadline. Euronews reported that the EU’s goods trade deficit with China has reached about €1 billion a day. The negotiations cover electric vehicles and broader market access. China rejected the EU’s proposal for voluntary export limits on electric cars, while Beijing has said any settlement must comply with World Trade Organization rules. European leaders expect Šefčovič to report concrete progress ahead of an EU summit scheduled for Oct. 15-16. EU officials have warned that a lack of results could increase support for tougher measures.
business.image_alt: EU presses China to curb exports as trade talks open in Beijing

business.title: Economists expect India’s central bank to raise rates again in December
business.summary: Economists expect the Reserve Bank of India to raise interest rates again in December. Bloomberg reported forecasts of successive increases into next year as inflation pressures broaden. HSBC and Goldman Sachs also expect a December hike, CNBC reported. The forecasts follow the RBI’s Oct. 7 increase, which raised its b
business.content: Economists expect the Reserve Bank of India to raise interest rates again in December. Bloomberg reported forecasts of successive increases into next year as inflation pressures broaden. HSBC and Goldman Sachs also expect a December hike, CNBC reported. The forecasts follow the RBI’s Oct. 7 increase, which raised its benchmark rate to 5.5% and shifted its policy stance to “calibrated tightening.” August inflation reached 4.82%, exceeding the RBI’s 4% target for a third consecutive month, while higher oil costs and a weak rupee add pressure. Governor Sanjay Malhotra ruled out near-term rate cuts and said the next move would depend on how conditions evolve.
business.image_alt: Economists expect India’s central bank to raise rates again in December

business.title: Watchdog urges OpenAI to pause ChatGPT for Teens over safeguard failures
business.summary: Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute rated OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Teens an “Unacceptable Risk” on Oct. 7 after testing more than 4,000 prompts. It said safeguards failed to alert linked parents to crisis conversations and often did not direct teen users to professional help. The watchdog urged OpenAI to stop ma
business.content: Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute rated OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Teens an “Unacceptable Risk” on Oct. 7 after testing more than 4,000 prompts. It said safeguards failed to alert linked parents to crisis conversations and often did not direct teen users to professional help. The watchdog urged OpenAI to stop marketing the product and bar under-18s from ChatGPT until its protections are shown to work. OpenAI disputed the findings, saying much of the testing may have taken place before parental controls were fully activated. Common Sense Media said some test accounts had been linked long enough for the controls to activate and stood by its results. OpenAI also said its teen users spent an average of less than 15 minutes a day on the service and used it mainly for learning. ChatGPT for Teens launched in August.
business.image_alt: Watchdog urges OpenAI to pause ChatGPT for Teens over safeguard failures

business.title: UK court overturns five Barclays traders’ rate-rigging convictions
business.summary: London’s Court of Appeal on Oct. 7 quashed the convictions of five former Barclays traders — Jay Merchant, Jonathan Mathew, Philippe Moryoussef, Alex Pabon and Colin Bermingham — convicted between 2016 and 2019 over alleged manipulation of Libor or Euribor. The rulings followed the UK Supreme Court’s 2025 decision to o
business.content: London’s Court of Appeal on Oct. 7 quashed the convictions of five former Barclays traders — Jay Merchant, Jonathan Mathew, Philippe Moryoussef, Alex Pabon and Colin Bermingham — convicted between 2016 and 2019 over alleged manipulation of Libor or Euribor. The rulings followed the UK Supreme Court’s 2025 decision to overturn the convictions of former traders Tom Hayes and Carlo Palombo after finding errors in jury instructions. The Serious Fraud Office did not contest the five appeals. The benchmarks influenced borrowing costs and financial products, including mortgages, pensions and savings. Libor was abolished at the end of 2024. The traders received prison terms, including an eight-year sentence for Moryoussef, who was sentenced in his absence. Former Deutsche Bank trader Christian Bittar’s appeal is scheduled for Oct. 9, and the SFO is contesting it. Former Barclays trader Peter Johnson also hopes to appeal.
business.image_alt: UK court overturns five Barclays traders’ rate-rigging convictions

business.title: Fed officials link data center boom to rising prices and power demand
business.summary: Federal Reserve officials have identified the data-center boom as a factor pushing prices higher, as electricity demand from artificial-intelligence computing adds pressure to energy costs. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly’s view on whether further rate increases are needed depends on how economic and energy shock
business.content: Federal Reserve officials have identified the data-center boom as a factor pushing prices higher, as electricity demand from artificial-intelligence computing adds pressure to energy costs. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly’s view on whether further rate increases are needed depends on how economic and energy shocks develop. A report cited by SolarQuarter puts U.S. grid congestion costs above $12 billion and calls for grid modernization, while energy-industry coverage describes data centers’ growing need for large, reliable power supplies. The Fed’s next policy decisions will depend in part on how those price pressures evolve.
business.image_alt: Fed officials link data center boom to rising prices and power demand

business.title: Trump allows highway use of red-dyed diesel through December
business.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order allowing highway use of red-dyed diesel, normally reserved for off-road equipment, through Dec. 31 and deferring the federal diesel excise tax of 24.4 cents per gallon. The order does not eliminate the tax obligation: Treasury guidance will determine whether drivers coul
business.content: President Donald Trump signed an executive order allowing highway use of red-dyed diesel, normally reserved for off-road equipment, through Dec. 31 and deferring the federal diesel excise tax of 24.4 cents per gallon. The order does not eliminate the tax obligation: Treasury guidance will determine whether drivers could later owe the deferred amount, and state restrictions still apply. The national average diesel price was about $6.30 a gallon on Oct. 7, more than 70% higher than a year earlier, as fuel supply disruptions linked to the Iran conflict and reduced Russian exports tightened supplies. Experts say the order will not add fuel to the market, and inconsistent state rules, limited access to red-dyed diesel and uncertainty over future tax bills could limit savings. The measure expires at year’s end, and Treasury guidance on deferred taxes is pending.
business.image_alt: Trump allows highway use of red-dyed diesel through December

science.title: Algae fueled by penguin guano darken Antarctic snow and speed melting
science.summary: A study of more than 100 snow samples from part of Antarctica found higher phosphate levels—nutrients associated with penguin and seabird droppings—in snow turned green by algae. Researchers say guano fertilizes dense algae blooms along the Antarctic Peninsula, while penguins spread nutrients as they walk over the snow
science.content: A study of more than 100 snow samples from part of Antarctica found higher phosphate levels—nutrients associated with penguin and seabird droppings—in snow turned green by algae. Researchers say guano fertilizes dense algae blooms along the Antarctic Peninsula, while penguins spread nutrients as they walk over the snow. Rising temperatures are expanding snow algae habitat along Antarctic coasts. The green growth darkens the snow, increasing solar energy absorption and accelerating melt. Researchers warn that models projecting the spread of ice-free ground may underestimate melting if they omit these biological effects. The study was published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences.
science.image_alt: Algae fueled by penguin guano darken Antarctic snow and speed melting

science.title: WMO forecasts record-strength El Niño to peak in December
science.summary: The World Meteorological Organization says the El Niño established in the tropical Pacific will intensify through the end of 2026. Sea-surface temperature anomalies in the central and eastern Pacific are forecast to reach about 3.7°C above normal in October-December, with the event likely to peak around December. The W
science.content: The World Meteorological Organization says the El Niño established in the tropical Pacific will intensify through the end of 2026. Sea-surface temperature anomalies in the central and eastern Pacific are forecast to reach about 3.7°C above normal in October-December, with the event likely to peak around December. The WMO puts the likelihood of the event lasting through February 2027 at nearly 100% and says it could be among the strongest since at least 1950. The previous Niño 3.4 anomaly record was 2.6°C in 2015-16. El Niño shifts winds and rainfall, increasing the risk of heat, drought and flooding in different regions. The WMO forecasts wetter-than-normal conditions in the Greater Horn of Africa, parts of Central and East Asia, northern parts of the Arabian Peninsula, parts of North America and southeastern South America, and drier conditions in the Indian subcontinent, southern Central America, parts of the Caribbean and northwestern South America. Human-driven climate change does not cause the natural climate pattern, but El Niño releases heat stored in the ocean and can compound the effects of a warmer baseline. In California, officials are preparing for coastal flooding, erosion, intense rain and debris flows. Forecasters caution that a strong El Niño changes the likelihood of such conditions but does not determine exact weather outcomes.
science.image_alt: WMO forecasts record-strength El Niño to peak in December

science.title: Hurricane Isaias targets Gulf Coast after quiet Atlantic season
science.summary: Isaias became the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 late Wednesday, with forecasters projecting landfall along the U.S. Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday. The storm could bring damaging winds, storm surge and heavy rain from southeastern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle, with flash flooding possible. The Nation
science.content: Isaias became the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 late Wednesday, with forecasters projecting landfall along the U.S. Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday. The storm could bring damaging winds, storm surge and heavy rain from southeastern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle, with flash flooding possible. The National Hurricane Center warned that the exact track and timing remained uncertain. Isaias is the ninth named storm of the season but the first to reach hurricane strength. Forecasters linked the notably quiet Atlantic period to a strong El Niño, which increases wind shear over the Caribbean and Atlantic. Waters of about 30 to 31 degrees Celsius and limited wind shear where Isaias formed helped it intensify, though increasing shear farther north may limit further strengthening. Florida and Alabama declared emergencies, Gulf oil producers suspended some output and Gulf Shores canceled its weekend National Shrimp Festival.
science.image_alt: Hurricane Isaias targets Gulf Coast after quiet Atlantic season

science.title: Study finds diverse Neanderthal wooden tools at Barcelona site
science.summary: Researchers catalogued 597 wooden remains and imprints dating to roughly 62,000 to 42,000 years ago at Abric Romaní, a Neanderthal site near Barcelona. They identified 13 objects, including possible spears and other pointed tools, bark containers, structural elements and a club-like object. The study brings together ev
science.content: Researchers catalogued 597 wooden remains and imprints dating to roughly 62,000 to 42,000 years ago at Abric Romaní, a Neanderthal site near Barcelona. They identified 13 objects, including possible spears and other pointed tools, bark containers, structural elements and a club-like object. The study brings together evidence previously examined separately. Newer 3D recording methods allowed researchers to reconstruct samples more quickly and conduct a broader analysis. The researchers said the repeated presence of different wooden objects across archaeological layers suggests woodworking was part of everyday technology, rather than limited to exceptional weapons. Excavations continue, and researchers say they keep finding new imprints as they expose more layers.
science.image_alt: Study finds diverse Neanderthal wooden tools at Barcelona site

science.title: Apollo software pioneer Margaret Hamilton dies at 90
science.summary: Margaret Hamilton, who led the development of onboard software for NASA’s Apollo missions, died Sept. 30 at age 90, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology said. Her team’s code guided Apollo spacecraft, including during the 1969 lunar landing, and was designed to keep mission-critical operations running when the onb
science.content: Margaret Hamilton, who led the development of onboard software for NASA’s Apollo missions, died Sept. 30 at age 90, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology said. Her team’s code guided Apollo spacecraft, including during the 1969 lunar landing, and was designed to keep mission-critical operations running when the onboard computer became overloaded. Hamilton joined MIT in 1959, and MIT hired her as its Apollo project’s first programmer in 1965. By 1968, she was assistant director overseeing the Command and Service Module software team, with more than 400 people working on Apollo software. The field was still new, and Hamilton helped establish software engineering as a discipline. After leaving MIT in the 1970s, she founded software companies and continued her work in computing; MIT says she authored more than 130 publications. President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016, and NASA chief Jared Isaacman described her as a pioneer whose work helped make Apollo possible.
science.image_alt: Apollo software pioneer Margaret Hamilton dies at 90

science.title: Three scientists win 2026 Nobel as optogenetic vision therapy enters review
science.summary: Three scientists whose work established optogenetics won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for a method that lets researchers use light to control genetically modified cells. Researchers use the technique in neuroscience experiments and are also testing whether it can restore some vision by making survivin
science.content: Three scientists whose work established optogenetics won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for a method that lets researchers use light to control genetically modified cells. Researchers use the technique in neuroscience experiments and are also testing whether it can restore some vision by making surviving retinal cells respond to light. The clinical evidence remains limited. A 2021 report described one blind patient who regained the ability to identify and locate some objects using specialized goggles, but did not regain normal sight. Separately, U.S. regulators accepted Nanoscope Therapeutics’ application for its MOGENRY therapy on Sept. 9, and Japan accepted an application for priority review on Oct. 1; neither acceptance constitutes approval. The Nobel-winning method and the company’s treatment are distinct developments; the treatment remains under regulatory review.
science.image_alt: Three scientists win 2026 Nobel as optogenetic vision therapy enters review

science.title: Climate-linked krill shifts tied to 63% drop in Zavodovski chinstraps
science.summary: Zavodovski Island’s chinstrap penguin population fell 63%, from an estimated 1.09 million breeding birds in 2011 to about 402,000 in 2025, according to a British Antarctic Survey-led study published in Current Biology. The island in the South Sandwich Islands has lost its distinction as home to the world’s largest peng
science.content: Zavodovski Island’s chinstrap penguin population fell 63%, from an estimated 1.09 million breeding birds in 2011 to about 402,000 in 2025, according to a British Antarctic Survey-led study published in Current Biology. The island in the South Sandwich Islands has lost its distinction as home to the world’s largest penguin colony; Cape Adare in the Ross Sea now holds that title, researchers say. Researchers say climate-driven changes in the Southern Ocean food web are the leading explanation. Chinstraps rely heavily on Antarctic krill and forage in cooler waters northwest of the island. As the ocean warms, krill have shifted south, beyond the birds’ feeding range. The team found a steady decline before and after Mount Curry’s 2016 eruption and considered the volcano unlikely to be the main cause. The researchers warn that the trend may affect chinstrap populations beyond Zavodovski and say the species may warrant reassessment of its current “Least Concern” status. A field expedition reached the remote island in 2023. Researchers combined drone and aerial surveys, satellite imagery and tracking data to assess changes through 2025.
science.image_alt: Climate-linked krill shifts tied to 63% drop in Zavodovski chinstraps

science.title: Vienna and Beijing teams demonstrate first working thorium nuclear clocks
science.summary: Teams in Vienna and Beijing have built the first working nuclear clocks, using lasers to drive an energy transition in thorium-229 nuclei embedded in calcium fluoride crystals. The devices use nuclear transitions as a timing reference rather than the electron transitions used by conventional atomic clocks. Both are pro
science.content: Teams in Vienna and Beijing have built the first working nuclear clocks, using lasers to drive an energy transition in thorium-229 nuclei embedded in calcium fluoride crystals. The devices use nuclear transitions as a timing reference rather than the electron transitions used by conventional atomic clocks. Both are prototypes and neither yet surpasses the best atomic clocks, which can lose or gain only about one second over billions of years. The Tsinghua University clock in Beijing showed about six times lower frequency instability than the Vienna system. Measurements from two independently produced Chinese crystals agreed at the 10^-13 level. Vienna researchers also used their clock to search for ultralight dark matter. The experiment found no evidence of it, but constrained possible dark-matter interactions at a level comparable to results from leading atomic clocks. Researchers say their next steps are to improve laser power, crystal quality and signal-to-noise performance. The teams’ studies appeared in Nature on Oct. 7. Proposed future uses include navigation, communications and precision tests of fundamental physics.
science.image_alt: Vienna and Beijing teams demonstrate first working thorium nuclear clocks

sports.title: NBA announcer Mike Breen apologizes after LeBron denies Embiid practice story
sports.summary: NBA broadcaster Mike Breen apologized Wednesday, Oct. 7, after LeBron James disputed Breen’s on-air account that James had reprimanded Philadelphia 76ers teammate Joel Embiid for arriving late to practice. Breen shared the anecdote during the Sixers’ 120-97 preseason win over the New York Knicks on Monday, saying it ca
sports.content: NBA broadcaster Mike Breen apologized Wednesday, Oct. 7, after LeBron James disputed Breen’s on-air account that James had reprimanded Philadelphia 76ers teammate Joel Embiid for arriving late to practice. Breen shared the anecdote during the Sixers’ 120-97 preseason win over the New York Knicks on Monday, saying it came from someone he trusted. James wrote on Instagram the next day that Embiid “ain’t been late” and urged people to stop spreading lies. Breen said he intended to praise James’s early leadership but accepted James’s denial and apologized for bringing unwanted attention to Embiid. Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Embiid had been working hard and performing well in camp. Philadelphia’s new lineup features James alongside Embiid and Jaylen Brown. The Sixers are scheduled to visit the Brooklyn Nets on Thursday, Oct. 8.

sports.title: NFL clears drink-themed celebrations after reversing Juszczyk and Ferguson fines
sports.summary: The NFL and NFL Players Association said on Oct. 7 that gestures imitating drinking a beverage will not draw a penalty or fine, after the league reversed fines against 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson. The league fined Juszczyk $14,926 for a celebration it interpreted as chugging beer an
sports.content: The NFL and NFL Players Association said on Oct. 7 that gestures imitating drinking a beverage will not draw a penalty or fine, after the league reversed fines against 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson. The league fined Juszczyk $14,926 for a celebration it interpreted as chugging beer and Ferguson $13,611 for a similar gesture. Both players said their celebrations referred to juice or Gatorade, and the league rescinded both fines. The joint guidance still allows discipline for gestures depicting violence, smoking, drug use or sexual content. It also says players should receive a warning when conduct falls into a gray area. NFLPA president JC Tretter said the union had sought clearer rules and supported education before punishment; the league said the guidance gives players greater clarity.

sports.content: Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement Tuesday after 14 NFL seasons, saying he needed to focus on his mental health and that his personal and family priorities had changed. On Wednesday’s First Take, ESPN host Stephen A. Smith questioned why Johnson stepped away four games into the season. After co-panelist Kimberly Martin challenged his remarks, Smith said he was not making light of mental-health issues and later apologized on his SiriusXM radio show. Smith said he had been discussing the Eagles’ difficult and chaotic situation, not Johnson’s mental health, but fans and sports media figures criticized both his original comments and his apology. Johnson said he wanted to play one final season but felt he owed his teammates, coaches, organization and fans his full commitment. He concluded that he could not make that commitment now.

Infantino is seeking a fourth term but faces opposition after FIFA abandoned a plan to bring private investors into a commercial entity ti
sports.content: Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega says he will run against Gianni Infantino in FIFA’s 2027 presidential election, becoming the first declared challenger to the incumbent. Infantino is seeking a fourth term but faces opposition after FIFA abandoned a plan to bring private investors into a commercial entity tied to World Cup rights. Several national associations have withdrawn their support. Vega, 55, says he wants to reform FIFA’s governance, restore trust and reunite football’s stakeholders. He retired in 2004 and later worked in finance. Candidates need backing from at least five of FIFA’s 211 member federations, a nomination by an association and approval through an eligibility review. The election is expected at the FIFA Congress next March. Candidates must meet the nomination criteria by November 18. UEFA says it intends to present an alternative candidate but had not settled on one ahead of its October governance discussions.

Rahm and the tour are negotiating a separation agreement; his lawyer said the golfer could pursue legal action if they fail to reach a deal. Rahm, one of
sports.content: Jon Rahm will not play in LIV Golf’s planned 2027 relaunch after rejecting its proposed terms as “unacceptable,” his lawyer told a U.S. bankruptcy court on October 7. Rahm and the tour are negotiating a separation agreement; his lawyer said the golfer could pursue legal action if they fail to reach a deal. Rahm, one of LIV’s most prominent players, is set to leave as the tour reorganizes after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund stopped backing the circuit. LIV filed for Chapter 11 protection in September, estimating liabilities of $500 million to $1 billion. New investor BC Partners Credit has offered up to $300 million to support a 2027 season, subject to court approval. Rahm’s departure is not yet final. The court extended LIV’s deadline to negotiate with players until October 25, and his lawyer said a separation agreement could be presented at a November 5 hearing. Rahm remains a DP World Tour member, but his next tour destination has not been confirmed.

sports.content: Senior figures in English football are concerned Manchester City could play in next season’s Champions League even if relegated domestically. Winning this season’s competition would qualify them as holders, and there is no automatic mechanism to bar a club that qualifies on sporting merit. UEFA is monitoring City’s appeal and will wait for the Premier League process to finish before deciding whether to open its own case. The concern centres on UEFA licensing. The FA issues licences through a process delegated to the Premier League, but eligibility is assessed on current information rather than historical breaches or sanctions. Football figures quoted by the BBC say the licensing question has been raised, while the Premier League sanction hearing has not yet been scheduled. Separately, rival club executives reportedly want penalties covering both past seasons and City’s future, but disagree over stripping titles. TalkSPORT presenter Alan Brazil has floated a 60-point deduction, describing it as unconfirmed information rather than a decided sanction. City deny wrongdoing and have appealed. A three-person panel is expected to hear the appeal for up to 12 weeks, with a decision due within 30 days of its conclusion.

sports.title: Australia return to South Africa for Tests with title race at stake

South Africa are the reigning World Test Championship winners, while Australia lead the current 2025–27 standings; both are targeting another p
sports.content: Australia and South Africa begin a three-Test series at Durban’s Kingsmead on Friday, October 9, their first Test meeting in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. South Africa are the reigning World Test Championship winners, while Australia lead the current 2025–27 standings; both are targeting another place in the final. The hosts won the recent one-day series 2-1, and conditions at Kingsmead could put spin bowlers in focus. South Africa are assessing whether fast bowler Kagiso Rabada has recovered from a hamstring injury, while Australia will be without all-rounder Cameron Green, who has been ruled out with an abdominal strain. Australia also arrive after a home Test defeat by Bangladesh in August.
